subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & GPU packing recommendations for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & proposed HW scenarios (initial plan)

Maria — following up on our call, attaching a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on performance benchmarking and a proposed closure timeline so procurement and engineering can align. High level summary below; full MAP attached (see attachments).

Goals (what we want to validate)
- Latency: Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target <= 120ms for single-stream interactive flows at 2-3 token generation start (measured P50/P95/P99).
- Throughput: Sustained token/s per GPU for batched inference (2048-context, typical batch sizes 8-32).
- Concurrency: End-to-end behavior at 8, 16, 32 concurrent sessions per model instance.
- Cost/pack density: Compare per-token unit cost across A100, H100, L40S with MIG vs full-GPU packing.

Planned HW scenarios (to be executed by Redwood perf team)
1) Full-GPU single-instance: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40S-48GB (quantized and non-quantized where supported).
2) MIG-style packing: 4-way and 7-way partitions (where applicable) on A100/H100 to measure density vs latency tradeoffs.
3) Mixed fleet: H100 for low-latency paths + L40S for high-throughput batch jobs.

Benchmark structure & instrumentation
- Harness: perf-runner v2 (tags: MAP-ACME-2026), workload replay from your anonymized production traces (sample subset we discussed).
- Metrics: TTFT (first token), per-token latency, tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, memory/KV cache behavior, GPU utilization, power.
- Eval variants: cold-start (empty KV cache) and warmed KV cache; quantized int8 vs fp16 where applicable.

Schedule (proposed)
- Aug 17–21: confirm traces, finalize test permutations.
- Aug 24–25: Redwood runs baseline A100/H100/L40S full-GPU and 4-way MIG.
- Aug 27: submit preliminary results and MAP update.
- Aug 30: deliver final perf summary and suggested fleet packing + recommendation for Dedicated capacity sizing.

Deliverables
- CSV with raw metrics + parsed summary (attached).
- MAP PDF with acceptance criteria and committed close dates (attached).
- Recommendation: minimal fleet to meet TTFT P95 SLA (we'll propose both conservative and aggressive sizing).

Next steps
- Please confirm schedule and provide the final sample trace export (S3 link or Drive). Also loop in procurement contact to align on a decision window — we recommend committing to a Dedicated trial by 2026-09-22 to hit your Q4 integration deadline.

Attachments: 20260830-map-acme.pdf (MAP + acceptance criteria)

Thanks — Lauren
--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — this looks good. A couple of clarifications before we sign off on the timeline:
1) For our low-latency interactive product, TTFT P95 must be <= 150ms (we can accept P99 up to 300ms). Can you show both P95 and P99?
2) MIG: our infra team prefers high-density packing for most customers, but we need a clear statement on P99 tail penalties per partition (we're sensitive to outliers).
3) Could you include L40S quantized runs (the partner said they saw good cost/latency tradeoffs last quarter)?

Procurement (cc) — Maria Lopez (product), this is the MAP/work plan. Procurement, please flag any contractual blockers for the 9/22 commit window.

Maria

Quick technical notes from the perf team (cc Neha who will run the experiment):
- We'll run both P95 and P99 sweeps, and report cold vs warm KV cache measurements. P99 often shows a 1.6–2.5x degradation when using MIG packing depending on model size and sequence length. We'll quantify per-partition sizes (4-way, 7-way).
- L40S: we'll include int8 quantized runs for L40S and H100 (where toolchain allows). Expect L40S int8 to be competitive in throughput but slightly worse TTFT for tiny-burst interactive sessions due to memory-copy overheads.
- Perf harness: we'll use perf-runner v2 + prometheus scrape + internal trace IDs so results map to your trace lines for audit.
- Cost modeling: we'll attach cost-per-1M-token approximations under the three packing scenarios (full GPU, 4-way MIG, 7-way MIG).

Operational ask: Maria, we'll need the 48-hour anonymized trace export (S3 link) and a list of your top-10 query templates. If you can send those by Friday (Aug 21), we can keep the Aug 24 run.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Performance

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP update & perf summary (final) — recommendation to mix H100 + L40S for closure

Maria / Procurement — attached is the final perf summary and our MAP update (attachments: 20260830-acme-perf-summary.csv, 20260830-map-acme.pdf). High-level findings below (results from Aug 24–27 runs).

High level results (selected)
- TTFT (interactive, warmed KV cache, 4-token warm prompt): H100 (fp16): P50=48ms, P95=68ms, P99=120ms; L40S (int8): P50=55ms, P95=75ms, P99=170ms; A100 (fp16): P50=62ms, P95=92ms, P99=150ms.
- Throughput (sustained tokens/sec per GPU, 2048-context, batch size 16): H100=4200 tok/s, L40S=3600 tok/s, A100=3100 tok/s.
- MIG packing density: 4-way MIG on A100 showed ~3.6x effective instance density for small models but introduced a P99 latency penalty of ~1.9x vs full-GPU for interactive flows. 7-way partitioning increased density but P99 penalties exceeded our acceptance threshold for interactive paths.
- Cost delta (ballpark): per-1M-token cost H100 < L40S < A100 when running critical low-latency workloads because H100's higher throughput reduces amortized cost, but for heavy batch embedding workloads L40S gives best $/token when quantized. Full CSV has per-scenario numbers.

Recommendation (short)
- Immediate: commit to a mixed fleet for pilot — H100-backed pool for interactive, latency-sensitive traffic and L40S-backed pool for batched/embedding work. Avoid 7-way MIG for interactive SLA routes; 4-way MIG is acceptable for asynchronous batch jobs.
- Sizing: to meet your P95 SLA for projected Q4 load (per our forecast in MAP PDF), we recommend initially reserving: 6 H100s (interactive) + 8 L40S (batch) and enabling autoscale. This is conservative and supports your growth with headroom. Detailed sizing spreadsheet in the MAP PDF and CSV.

Next steps & close timeline
- Procurement decision window: please confirm by 2026-09-22 for a Sept deploy of Dedicated trial.
- Onboarding: Redwood will run a 2-week soak of your live non-prod traffic (we'll coordinate dates).
- Contracts: procurement, please review the Attached MAP + our standard Dedicated terms; we flagged the SLA window in the PDF.

Attachments referenced (stubs):
- 20260830-acme-perf-summary.csv — raw metrics + parsed per-scenario costs
- 20260830-map-acme.pdf — MAP with acceptance criteria, milestones, and decision signoff page

Action items
- Maria: confirm decision window (due 9/22) and provide SOW reviewer contact.
- Procurement: share any required PO info or legal blockers.
- Redwood (Neha/Karthik): schedule the Dedicated pilot and finalize perf run deck for your infra team.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Lauren
